title: The email worker left the API
subtitle: Example · illustrative data · 2026
summary: The API answers Stripe before sending; the worker owns the retry.

views.title: Cover
views.summary: An architecture decision in six slides.
views.notes: Start with the problem, not the solution. The Stripe webhook waited for SMTP before answering. The whole deck fits in one sentence: the API answers before the email.

views.title: The problem
views.summary: The Stripe response waited for SMTP.
views.notes: An email provider timeout became a Stripe retry. There was no job; the API owned the failure.

views.title: Synchronous sending couples three failures
views.summary: The response waits for the provider; the retry starts on the other side.
views.notes: Follow the error edge: SMTP is slow, the API does not answer, Stripe retries. Postgres and the provider sit in the same response.

views.title: p95 fell from 2.4 s to 180 ms
views.summary: After the worker, the API answers before SMTP.
views.notes: The chart is illustrative, but the shape matters: the drop happens at the worker deploy, not at the volume. The 300 ms target is the reference line.

blocks.title: p95 of the webhook per month
blocks.caption: Illustrative data, not a production measurement.

views.title: A single queue won on isolation and cost
views.summary: Retry left the API; the single queue won by a small margin.
views.notes: The queue per channel isolates more, but doubles the operational cost. The single queue already takes SMTP out of the response and keeps one worker. The weights come from a team of four: isolation first, cost next.

blocks.title: Three options, three criteria
blocks.weightBasis: Isolation weighs most: an email failure cannot take down the webhook. Cost reflects the team of four; latency breaks the tie.

single.raw: one failure does not affect the API

recommendation.rationale: The queue per channel isolates more but doubles the cost; the single queue already takes SMTP out of the response.

views.title: The API answers before the email
views.summary: The worker owns the retry; Stripe gets 200 in under 200 ms.
views.notes: Close on the contract: the API only marks the order and enqueues. Delivery, retries and provider failures stay in the worker.
